rollup.choiceIndicatorCensus: HEADLINE: 19 of the 49 code-block diagrams carry choice indicators in the printed standard. The markdown preserved them in exactly ONE (PICTURE clause Format 1, line 20247, p.471). **18 of 19 printed choice-indicator groups were dropped in transcription — a 95% loss rate.** The single surviving instance is why the corpus-wide `|` count was 1. Of the 18 losses, 17 are DECISION-CHANGING (the 18th, PICTURE, was not lost); every dropped group either (a) turned a "one or more, any order" BRACE-with-bars into an exclusive select-exactly-one, or (b) turned a "zero or more, any order" BRACKET-with-bars into a zero-or-one. Fourteen of the losses are the positive/negative conditional-phrase pair (ON SIZE ERROR/NOT, ON EXCEPTION/NOT), i.e. the exact case where a markdown-only reader would conclude the standard forbids writing both branches on one statement. Three further losses are not conditional phrases at all and are easy to miss: PROGRAM-ID `COMMON`+`{INITIAL|RECURSIVE}` (p.287), INITIALIZE `category-name` list of 13 (p.667), SORT `COLLATING SEQUENCE FOR ALPHANUMERIC`/`FOR NATIONAL` (p.775), plus DISPLAY Format 2's `AT LINE/COLUMN` brace (p.640) which carries bars AND is separate from that statement's exception-phrase bars — that diagram lost two distinct choice-indicator groups.
